question_text: Would you like to assess just one specific situation, or compare two cases?
question_explanation:
In a "single case" assessment, you only provide data on the so called "reference case." This is then compared to an implicit "comparison case" of "no walking or cycling."
In a "two cases" assessment you have to specify both cases, the "reference case" and the "comparison case." Typical examples are "before and after" an intervention, or comparisons of alternative "scenarios A and B."
For more guidance on how this selection affects the calculation, see here.
level_hint: Only information on the reference case will be required

question_text: What is the year for your comparison case?
Over how many years should the impacts be calculated?
question_hint:
Note that the data you will enter for the reference year and the comparison year will define the "contrast" (i.e. the difference or change) in active travel that you will assess, while the assessment time below will define the duration over which the impacts will be calculated. You can quantify the resulting impacts over any period of time, e.g. 10 or 30 years. In addition, resuls will always be presented per one year as well.
Further note that the reference year does not count towards the assessment. E.g. a 10 year assessment comparing reference year 2020 to comparison year 2030 will add impacts of 2021-2030. If the comparison year is before the reference year, the assessment will start with the first year after the comparison year.
Learn more about how HEAT handles years here.

For example, if after a particular measure (e.g. a foot path) has been implemented it may take 5 years for usage to reach a steady state, this figure should be changed to 5. The default value has been set to 1 year, i.e. the full amount of active travel is considered in year 1 of the assessment already. If you are coomparing two steady-state situations and do not want to take into account any take-up time, set it to 1.
